title: President Donald Trump to miss United States’ opening World Cup game, Andrew Giuliani says
content:
Andrew Giuliani, the World Cup task force’s CEO, has confirmed President Donald Trump will not attend the United States men’s national team’s opening game of the tournament against Paraguay on Friday.

The Athletic reported on Wednesday that President Trump was not planning to be at the fixture at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, California. The State Department issued a release to say Secretary of State Marco Rubio will attend the game, along with Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy and Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin.

Giuliani confirmed the news in an interview Thursday, citing Trump’s schedule as the reason for his non-attendance, but said he expected the U.S. president to become more engaged in the World Cup over the course of the tournament.

“He’s not going to end up attending the opening game,” Giuliani told UK radio station TalkSport. “As we’ve said, his scheduling is tight. But I know he’s going to be engaged throughout this World Cup.

“But the one thing, having known President Trump for now 30 years, what I can tell you is: expect the unexpected. Always expect a cliffhanger with him. Throughout the course of this tournament, it wouldn’t surprise me if we see him engage more and more with the World Cup.”

It is highly unusual for the head of state of a host nation to skip their team’s opening game at a men’s World Cup — Tamim bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, the Emir of Qatar, attended in 2022, President Vladimir Putin of Russia attended in 2018 and President Dilma Rousseff of Brazil attended in 2014.

President Claudia Sheinbaum of Mexico, however, was also not in attendance for her country’s opening game of the tournament, Thursday’s 2-0 win over South Africa. She instead chose to give away her ticket to Yolett Cervantes Cuaquehua, a young Indigenous woman who won a national contest held by the Mexican government to secure Sheinbaum’s VIP seat at Estadio Azteca. Sheinbaum was pictured celebrating Mexico’s goal from a fan park in Mexico City. She told reporters last month she does not intend to attend any matches at the tournament.

Trump has developed a strong relationship with FIFA president Gianni Infantino and received the FIFA Peace Prize at the World Cup draw in December.

He has attended a series of high-profile sporting events since returning to the White House, including Game 3 of the NBA Finals this week at Madison Square Garden in New York City, where he was booed by the crowd.

He has previously attended the Super Bowl in New Orleans; UFC fights in Miami and New Jersey; the Daytona 500; the NCAA Wrestling Championships in Philadelphia; the FIFA Club World Cup final at MetLife Stadium; and the U.S. Open men’s tennis final.
